sources.citation: Lobel, Jason William. 2013. Philippine and North Bornean languages: issues in description, subgrouping, and reconstruction. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa (hdl 10125/101972).
sources.note: Nothing for Talantang. 'Dusun Talantang' (DTlt) appears only in pronoun Table 4.13 (tika') and in lists of *J > g reflexes; the dissertation's accent discussion (8.2.9, Maranao chapter) concerns Philippine languages only.

sources.citation: Kroeger, Paul R. 1993. Kimaragang phonemics. In Boutin & Pekkanen (eds.), Phonological descriptions of Sabah languages, 31-45. Sabah Museum Monograph 4. (partial Rosetta Project scan, pp. 31-39)
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: Harvard print copy (Scan & Deliver or loan); the journal or volume is held, not the item itself: WID Offsite Storage P381.S23 P45 1993
sources.note: Describes Tandek Kimaragang [kqr], not Talantang; mentions a 'Kimaragang-Garo' sub-dialect (Kg. Longob, Masolog) which Kroeger 1985 identifies as Kimaragang of mixed Kimaragang/Garo descent, i.e. not the Talantang/Garo language. Its stress section (sec. 4) is not in the scan. Not usable for grm.

sources.citation: Kroeger, Paul R. 1985. Linguistic relations among the Dusunic groups in the Kota Marudu District. Borneo Research Bulletin 17(1): 31-46.
sources.note: Nothing. Sections 'Tinagas / Garo' and 'Kota Marudu Talantang' (PDF p.21) give ethnonyms, settlement history (Kg. Talantang founded by Talantang from the Sugut River) and lexicostatistics (83% cognate with Sugut Talantang, 85% with Parong, 80-81% with Tandek Kimaragang); only phonological remark in the article is Pitas vs Tandek Kimaragang voiced stops. The word 'stress' does not occur in the article.

sources.citation: King, Julie K. & John Wayne King (eds.) 1984. Languages of Sabah: a survey report. Pacific Linguistics C-78. Canberra: ANU. [Smith, 'The languages of Sabah: a tentative lexicostatistical classification' 1-49 (sec. 2.3.9.4.10 'Garo' = Talantang KM); King, 'The Rungus language' 283-296 (sec. 3.1.2); Banker & Banker, 'The Kadazan/Dusun language' 297-324 (sec. 3.4 'Garo language', Figs. 21-22)]
sources.note: Nothing. Lexicostatistics and intelligibility testing at Talantang KM ('The people from Talantang KM use the autonym Garo'); Banker & Banker sec. 3.4 establishes Garo as a language distinct from Kimaragang (<80% intelligibility). No phonology; 'stress'/'accent'/'penult' occur nowhere in the volume.
